chief_complaint: pain on outer elbow with wrist extension, Cozen positive
hpi_details: A 71-year-old male presents to the clinic with pain on outer elbow with wrist extension, cozen positive. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: thinks it may be tennis elbow
concerns: He is worried his grip will keep deteriorating and force him to give up his woodworking hobby.
expectations: He hopes to be fitted with a supportive arm strap and given prescription anti-inflammatory patches.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of lateral epicondylitis is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
Diagnosis is clinical: reproduce focal lateral-epicondyle pain with resisted wrist or middle-finger extension, but do not diagnose from Cozen testing alone.

Management may include activity modification, a progressive wrist-extensor loading program, and a trial of counterforce bracing when appropriate, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: pain on outer elbow with wrist extension, Cozen positive

Key HPI features: A 71-year-old male presents to the clinic with pain on outer elbow with wrist extension, cozen positive. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Examination should localize tenderness at or just distal to the lateral epicondyle; assess elbow and cervical range of motion, grip strength, sensation, and wrist/finger extension strength.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out lateral epicondylitis.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue strain without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as progressive wrist or finger weakness, fever with a hot swollen joint, recent significant trauma, or unexplained systemic symptoms.
management_principles: After excluding atypical causes, consider activity modification, progressive wrist-extensor loading, and a counterforce brace when appropriate; analgesic choice requires individual risk review.
Obtain further evaluation for diagnostic uncertainty, trauma, systemic features, progressive neurologic deficit, major functional limitation, or failure to improve with conservative care.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 128/78 mmHg, pulse 72 beats per minute, respiratory rate 14 breaths per minute, body temperature 36.6°C, oxygen saturation 98% on room air.
No erythema, swelling, warmth, or gross deformity of either elbow; marked focal tenderness over the right lateral epicondyle and common extensor tendon origin.
Resisted extension of the right wrist with elbow extended elicits sharp pain at the lateral epicondyle (positive Cozen test); motor strength 5/5 throughout bilaterally.
Intact light touch and pinprick sensation across C5 through T1 dermatomes bilaterally, with no numbness or paresthesias.
Biceps, brachioradialis, and triceps deep tendon reflexes are 2+ and symmetric bilaterally.
Full active and passive cervical range of motion without midline tenderness or radiating arm pain; Spurling test is negative.
No rashes, psoriatic plaques, tophi, nail pitting, or inflammatory lesions on the skin or extensor surfaces.
